properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 6 at 8:21AM CDT until October 7 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Nebraska...

Big Blue River At Beatrice affecting Gage County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Big Blue River at Beatrice.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Chautauqua Park begins to flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 AM CDT Tuesday the stage was 19.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 16.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:45 AM CDT Tuesday was 20.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage this
afternoon and continue falling to 4.7 feet Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.1
feet on 07/22/1978.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 830 PM CDT.

properties.areaDesc: Tampa Bay waters; Coastal waters from Englewood to Tarpon Springs FL out 20 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 6 at 4:10PM EDT until October 6 at 4:45PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description: SMWTBWThe National Weather Service in Tampa Bay Ruskin has issued a  * Special Marine Warning for... Tampa Bay waters... Coastal waters from Englewood to Tarpon Springs FL out 20 NM...  * Until 445 PM EDT.  * At 410 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing waterspouts was located 7 NM west of Anna Maria, or 7 NM west of Anna Maria Island, moving northeast at 5 knots.  HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 34 knots.  SOURCE...Radar indicated.  IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and suddenly higher waves.  * Locations impacted include... Manatee 3 Mile North Reef, Passage Key Inlet, Southwest Channel, Egmont Key, Anna Maria and Manatee 7 Mile North Reef.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

may already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the
warned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and
property.

These forecasts are based almost entirely on observed precipitation
as little to no additional precipitation is currently expected over
the next 24 to 48 hours.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued by late tonight.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 6 at 7:40AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor has risen into Minor Flood Stage and is
forecast to continue a steady rise through this week due to northerly
winds and repeated rounds of heavy rainfall across the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...From this morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 2.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:30 AM EDT Tuesday was 2.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river has risen to Minor Flood Stage at 2.3 feet
and is expected to continue rising through flood stage, reaching
2.7 feet late this week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.6
feet on 10/14/1996.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
